sections.title: Other
items: UI follow-ups: system mono, grid tail cells, dead shell state

sections.title: New
items: A new look. The terminal-style screens are gone: a sidebar lists Overview, your agents, History, Library and Settings (keys 1 to 8 always open the same place), and a top bar has Check and Update all. Everything is mouse-first, with the keyboard shortcuts as accelerators (`?` lists them). Neutral graphite with a matching light theme, the system font for text, and motion that follows Settings > Motion (#94, #102, #103, #105, #108, #109)

Overview answers "is my setup OK?" at the top: "Your setup works." or "Everything is set up.", with one line that counts only what is not zero. Each agent has a card, and the last update shows what changed and what was left for you, with Undo

Decisions are shown where they belong. A file you edited gets a card that says why Riggverk left it alone; Compare opens the side-by-side difference right there, and the two choices say what happens next. Nothing is written before you preview it, Enter never applies, and `y` or the Apply button does (#105, #107)

Codex settings: the table shows Riggverk's value next to yours for each key Riggverk manages. Keep mine keeps your value; Use Riggverk defaults sets only the keys that differ, after a preview, with a backup and Undo. Riggverk refuses instead of touching anything the preview didn't show (#99, #107)
History lists every update, also after a restart, with what changed, what was already current and what was left for you. Undo is offered on the newest one and always asks first (#98, #106)

Skill packs: put your own skills in `~/.config/riggverk/packs/<name>/skills/` and Riggverk installs them like its own, with backups and Undo. If a pack goes missing or can't be read, its skills stay installed until you choose Forget pack in the Library. Packs that others can write to are refused (#101, #104)

sections.title: Before you open it
items: Quit any older Riggverk that is still running before the first launch of this version. This release moves Riggverk's data folder, and two versions working at the same time could split it.

sections.title: New
items: Riggverk's own names now say Riggverk everywhere. The data folder moves from `~/.config/agent-workspace` to `~/.config/riggverk`, its state folder from `.agent-workspace/` to `.riggverk/`, and the markers in your rules files become `BEGIN RIGGVERK BASE` / `END RIGGVERK BASE`. Nothing moves when the app opens: the folder is renamed the first time Riggverk writes something, and your rules files get the new markers on their next update, with everything you wrote below END kept byte for byte. `RIGGVERK_WORKSPACE_PATH` and `RIGGVERK_BACKUP_DIR` replace the old variables, which still work. A saved custom folder is never moved. If the move cannot happen, Riggverk keeps working in the old folder and says why on the workspace row. Scripts or editors that open files in `~/.config/agent-workspace` need the new path, and going back to an older version after the move is not supported

Codex settings you changed on purpose can stay yours. When an enforced key in `~/.codex/config.toml` differs from Riggverk's value, such as `approvals_reviewer`, press `m` on the Codex config row: Riggverk keeps your value, stops reporting it as a conflict and never writes over it, while the other managed keys keep following Riggverk. Change the value again and it becomes a conflict again; press `m` once more to hand it back

First steps of the new look: a neutral graphite palette with no amber, a neutral light theme, and calmer review screens. Install previews, rules reviews, file conflicts and confirm dialogs are now cards that say what happens before you apply ("Preview first · Backed up · Undo any time"). Enter still never applies; `y` or the Apply button does (#89, #93)

sections.title: New
items: Claude Code can stop adding its attribution to your commits and pull requests. Turn on the `config` target on the Claude page, then Install. It sets `attribution.commit` and `attribution.pr` to `""` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, which removes the `Co-Authored-By` commit line and the "Generated with Claude Code" PR line. Every other setting in the file stays. If you already chose your own attribution, or the file has comments, Riggverk leaves it alone. The target is off by default, and `z` undoes it

Each harness page has a `security` group that shows which permission and sandbox settings in that harness's own config are risky, enforced or only advice, such as bypass mode, an open network or a missing sandbox. It only reads named settings, never shows their values, and never says a setup is safe: project config, profiles and command-line flags are not checked

New guide in Library > Docs > Security Baseline: per harness, what Riggverk enforces and what you have to do yourself, plus how to keep unknown repositories and production credentials away from your agents

sections.title: Fixes
items: A harness Riggverk has not installed anything into shows "not installed" again, even when Riggverk already manages another harness on the same computer. Before, it showed "update available"

The OpenCode critic in adversarial-implementation stops before the review when it would get any tool beyond reading, such as your own tools in `~/.config/opencode/tools/`, and names them so they can be denied

sections.title: Changes
items: Riggverk no longer keeps a copy of its bundle in your workspace folder (`~/.config/agent-workspace`). The Library and health read the bundle inside the app, and the folder now holds only Riggverk's state (`.agent-workspace/`), your personal docs (`docs/context/`) and anything you put there yourself

Old copies from earlier versions show on the `workspace` row as "N old copies to remove". Press `u` to review: every removal is listed per folder and backed up first, and `z` restores them. Nothing is removed at launch (#76, #78)
Files you edited, and files Riggverk cannot prove it wrote, are left in place and shown as "left in place". To keep a copy of everything, cancel the review, or press `z` after applying
The workspace view no longer shows the data folder's git branch or uncommitted changes; GIT_VERSIONING.md now covers versioning `docs/context/` only

sections.title: Fixes
items: Files that only early test builds shipped are also cleaned up when they are unchanged

sections.title: New
items: adversarial-review: a fresh read-only critic finds and verifies issues and reports them without fixing anything; plan mode and a separate list for issues that were already there
adversarial-test: an adversary writes failing tests that are then frozen, and the implementer may change only production code

adversarial-implementation v2: the critic is chosen by capability, every finding carries a proof the lead runs, at most three rounds with frozen tests and a final round that may only delete; a start line shows who plays each role and how to change it
Start the adversarial skills in plain words or with their slash command (#69, #71, #72)
OpenCode: a critic model row, so the adversarial skills' critic (inspector) can run a stronger model than the other subagents

sections.title: Fixes
items: Critics can no longer reach MCP tools such as Playwright, whether they run in OpenCode, Codex or Claude Code

Riggverk replaces Agent Workspace. Quit Agent Workspace, move Agent Workspace.app to the Trash and install Riggverk.app (see Install). Your settings and backups move to Riggverk's folder on the first launch.

sections.title: New
items: Copilot, Pi and Kilo as opt-in harnesses: rules block, skills and the Playwright MCP entry (#40, #41, #42)
One shared SKILL.md per skill, installed into each folder your harnesses read; see which copy each harness loads (#28, #30, #33, #34)
Resolve a conflicting skill or agent file: keep your version or take the bundled one (#44, #45)
Library: bundled items are read-only and come straight from the app; edit your personal docs and your own refinements below the rules base (#49, #52, #57)

OpenCode: version-aware health with CLI probes and lsp, model/small model/subagent model overrides, runtime rows that show what differs, warnings when other config files or env override the team settings, only the bundled tui.json keys are managed, XDG_CONFIG_HOME is followed (#31, #32, #54, #55, #60, #63)
What's new after each update
New skills: adversarial-implementation, security-audit, kretsverket-status-report (#19, #20, #21)
Master-detail pages, bracket buttons, apply progress and motion levels (#14, #17)

sections.title: Changed
items: Renamed to Riggverk; app data moves on first launch (#37, #39)
Prompt Builder, Brain Setup and the in-app release check are removed (#26, #27)
The workspace folder chooser is gone: a saved folder keeps working, and `R` resets to the default after a confirm
Playwright MCP 0.0.83 runs your installed Google Chrome; tools that web pages register (WebMCP) are off

sections.title: Fixes
items: OpenCode permissions match OpenCode 1.19.3: compound commands are checked part by part, and secret files are denied in bash however the path is written (#29, #65, #66)
The managed OpenCode config converges, and health compares with what Install writes (#51, #56)
The window opens centered at 1280x800, the boot lines clear the traffic lights, and the pane grid holds at large text (#13, #22, #38)
Codex delegation only when Codex is installed and logged in
The Playwright entry is added to an existing mcp.json
